titulo: How a space telescope sees: inside Webb
caption:
How do you see galaxies whose light left over 13 billion years ago? 🔭

The James Webb Space Telescope orbits about 1.5 million km from Earth. Its 6.5-meter mirror, built from 18 gold-coated segments, gathers faint infrared light and sends it to instruments that split it into detailed data. A sunshield keeps the telescope below -223°C so it can detect that heat-sensitive signal.
